title: I’ve never seen anything on stage as visually beautiful as Black Swan...
transcript: There are theater trips, and then there are theater pilgrimages, and finally getting to see Dave Malloy's Black Swan was definitely the latter. Literally insane that you need it now. Getting up to American Repertory Theater in Cambridge was certainly a journey. It included a blown tire, a triple A call, and switching cars with my sister. But it was incredibly vital that I got to see this musical because I genuinely can't think of a better match than Dave Malloy and Black Swan. Add in the fact that Jen Silverman wrote the book and Sonya Tayeh directed and choreographed it, I was fully already sad before anyone had been cast. If you've never seen Black Swan, it's about the competitive world of professional ballet and a young ballerina named Nina, who is cast as the lead in Swan Lake. And even though this is her dream, the pressure of that, both internally and externally, causes her grip on reality to fracture. It's a psychological thriller, at points deeply unsettling, and this musical captures all of it. Black Swan is built on movement and breath and. And for me, Sonia's choreography with Dave score just live in perfect harmony. Now, it's been a couple years since I've seen the movie, but they did make a couple of big changes, including changing the choreographer from a man to a woman, played by Amber Amand. I'm obsessed with this. A because I love Amber, and B because it strips the men from the Story and makes it more about Nina. Her ambition and her affectionism and her complicated feelings of jealousy and lust for Lily. Amber Raman just brings so much to the show. She commands the stage. She's so magnetic and obviously has the greatest voice. And Melanie Moore is the perfect Nina. She's a beautiful dancer. She can tell an entire story with just her movement. But she's not afraid to go to the dark place and bring everyone along with her. And this does go dark places. There is some incredible body horror in Black Swan. The illusions and the special effects, makeup and the costuming fine with this aging. And the score gives this feeling of like a fever dream that keeps you on edge. This show is just a huge swing, and to me, it really pays off. If you can get yourself to Cambridge, I think going to art is definitely worth the trip. And selfishly, I really hope this isn't the last we see of Black Swan, because I really wanna see it again.
